Part A:Basic Operations

A1 create v as the sequence 5,10,15 ..... 50 using seq().Print its length,sum and mean

```{r}
v <- seq(5:50)

length(5:50)
sum(5:50)
mean(5:50)
```
A2 Create w that repeats the vector c(1,2,3) four times and z that repeats each element of c(1,2,3) four times print both

```{r}
w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)

print(w)
print(z)
```

A3 Compute and print: the remainder if 17 divided by 5 the integer division of 17 by 5,2 to the power of 10 the square root of 144 and pi rounded to decimal.

```{r}
17 %% 5
17 %/% 5
2 ^ 10
sqrt(144)
round(pi,3)
```
A4 Given a <- c(2,4,6,8) and b <- c(1,3,5,7) print a + b,a * b the logical comparison a > b and dot product sum (a * b.)

```{r}
a <- c(2,4,5,8)
b <- c(1,3,5,7)
print(a + b)
print(a * b)
print(a > b)
print(sum(a * b))
```

Part B :Data Frames and Conditional Statements

B1 create a data frame students with 8 rows and these column (use stringsAsFactors = FALSE: sex is "M" OR "F")

```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  sex = c("M", "F", "M", "F", "M", "F", "M", "F"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

print(students)
```
B2 display the structure, dimension ,column name and summary of students.

```{r}

str(students)


dim(students)


colnames(students)


summary(students)
```

B3 add a column average = the mean of midterm and final for each student rounded to 1 decimal.

```{r}
students$midterm <- c(80, 85, 78, 90, 88, 75, 92, 84)

students$final <- c(85, 90, 82, 95, 89, 80, 94, 88)
students$average <- round(
  rowMeans(students[, c("midterm", "final")]),
  1
)

print(students)
```
B4 add a logical column passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 and attendance >=75

```{r}
students$attendance <- c(90, 85, 70, 95, 80, 75, 90, 88)

students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75

print(students)
```

B5 using ifelse() ,add a column standing with these value based on average:

."Honor" if average >= 90
."Good" if average >= (and below 90)
."Need Support" otherwise

```{r}

students$standing <- ifelse(
  students$average >= 90, "Honor",
  ifelse(students$average >= 70, "Good", "Need Support")
)

print(students)
```
B6 writea function classify(score )that uses as if / else if / else chain and return "Distinction"
for 85 or above "Merit" for 70 to 84 "Pass" FOR 50 TO 69 AND "Fail" below 50 test it with sapply(c(90,73,55,40),classify) and print the result.

```{r}

classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}


result <- sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)

print(result)
```
Part C rbind() and cbind()\

C1 create a data frame new_students with two student its column must match the original, including average,passed and standing, computed the same way:

.id 9 ines, F,section C,midterm 81,final 84,attendance 92
.id 10, Jamal,M,section A, midterm 70,final 68,attendance 80

```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


new_students$average <- round(
  rowMeans(new_students[, c("midterm", "final")]),
  1
)


new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 &
                       new_students$attendance >= 75


new_students$standing <- ifelse(
  new_students$average >= 90, "Honor",
  ifelse(new_students$average >= 70, "Good", "Need Support")
)

print(new_students)
```

c2 create the numeric vector quiz <-c(8,7,10,6,7,9,10,5,8,6) use cbind() to attach it to student_all as a column named quiz confirm the result is still a data frame with class()

```{r}
ls()
names(students)
names(new_students)

ncol(students)
ncol(new_students)

str(students)
str(new_students)

student_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)


student_all <- cbind(student_all, quiz = quiz)


print(student_all)


class(student_all)
```

c3 create the matrix  m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = student_all$final)
and use rbind to append a final row comtaining the column means,labelled "mean"

```{r}

m <- cbind(
  midterm = student_all$midterm,
  final = student_all$final
)

m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))


print(m)
```

c4 in the comment () (2-3 sentences) explain what rbind() produced if the the data frames have different column names and show output if you safelty catch it with tryCatch()
tryCatch(rbind(students , bad error = function(e) {message("rbind failed: ",conditionMessage(e));NULL})

```{r}
# rbind() combines data frames by matching their columns by position,
# but it requires the data frames to have the same column names.
# If the column names are different, rbind() produces an error.

tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)

students <- data.frame(id = c(1, 2), name = c("Ana", "Ben"))

bad <- data.frame(student_id = c(3, 4), fullname = c("Cara", "Dan"))

tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
```
